- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes in history.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting lag or failure to capture near-term downward pressure.
- Overreacts to recent high values (overshoots after spikes), then undercorrects — model tends to peak too high and then dip too low.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to smoothly decay toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10–15 days, then gradually drifts lower — suggests model doesn’t adjust for short-term volatility or seasonality.
- Model often fails to account for sudden drops in the last 3–5 days, especially when true outcome shows sharp declines after a plateau.
